opening.spoken: This record covers the claimed solution of Erdős problem #593: what has been claimed, what it rests on, and what would have to be checked by whom.

short_version.spoken: Erdős asked which finite 3-uniform hypergraphs must appear in every 3-uniform hypergraph of uncountable chromatic number, a five-hundred-dollar problem. In June and July 2026 two claimants, Eric Li and Samuil Petkov, each working with an AI system, listed proofs reaching the same characterisation, each with a Lean development. Two claims that agree is more than one, and still nobody independent has reported building either development or reading either argument. Everything here is open.

what_happened.spoken: The claim was pinned from the public record: the problem page, the proof-claims thread, and every artifact the claimants made public, by commit or hash. Nothing was run. The gaps that follow are the checks still owed.

Samuil Petkov listed a proof claim reaching the same characterisation, stating it had been checked by AI models and not by an expert. Eric Li listed his proof claim on the problem page. Eric Li's Lean repository reached its current commit. Samuil Petkov's repository reached its current commit, with a Lean formalisation under a formalization folder. The problem page lists two proof claims, neither marked accepted by the site. A third-party formalisation of the problem statement exists.

background.spoken: A 3-uniform hypergraph has chromatic number greater than aleph-null if its vertices cannot be coloured with countably many colours without a monochromatic edge. Which finite 3-uniform hypergraphs appear inside every such hypergraph? For ordinary graphs Erdős considered the question solved: uncountably chromatic graphs contain every finite bipartite graph but need not contain any fixed odd cycle.

background.spoken: The claim characterises the obligatory finite triple systems: after deleting isolated vertices, exactly the linear systems in which every hyperedge-node meets a bridge in the Levi graph and every Berge cycle has even length. The author states that the argument was checked by AI models several times and not by an expert, and that a formalisation was under way at submission; the repository now holds a Lean formalisation.

provenance.source: public record to 2026-11-14: the problem page, its proof-claims thread and the claimants' public artifacts, pinned in claim.yaml

background.spoken: The claim resolves problems 593 and 1177 together. The obligatory finite triple systems are exactly the class generated from private-vertex expansions of finite bipartite graphs by finite disjoint unions and one-point amalgamations, equivalently the linear systems with a bridge at every hyperedge-node of the Levi graph and only even Berge cycles. The proof uses an exact bridge-trace theorem for one-apex sequence lifts, and also constructs, for every uncountable cardinal, a linear triple system of exactly that chromatic number. The author states the paper was public on arXiv on June 23, 2026, before any other proof of 593 or 1177, and welcomes others to join the formalisation.
